invariants.rule: Core desktop abstractions remain independent of any specific machine, SSH topology, control backend, or deployment profile.
Project Control, Codex, telemetry, remote control, and host-specific semantics stay behind application or provider boundaries.
Terminal initialization has explicit ownership and restoration on normal and handled-error exits; terminal corruption is a serious defect.
An embedded interactive pane requires a mature VT terminal-state engine; a PTY alone is not an embedded terminal and txtDesk does not invent a fake emulator.
Do not stabilize a plugin ABI until multiple working applications provide evidence for the required extension boundary.
Python 3.12 or newer is the default implementation substrate; native extensions require a demonstrated low-level or performance need.
Use Textual as the current TUI foundation and do not build a redundant widget, layout, focus, or event framework underneath it.

tasks.objective: Validate unit tests, packaging and entry points, TUI smoke behavior, SSH and terminal compatibility, architecture boundaries, and user/developer documentation across the delivered project.

charter.objective: Deliver txtDesk as a portable text-mode desktop through bounded, dependency-ordered milestones.
boundaries: The core is host-agnostic and operates on the current terminal.
Applications and providers own external and machine-specific semantics.
No embedded terminal exists until a mature VT engine is deliberately integrated.
No stable plugin ABI exists during the early compiled-in application phase.
invariants: Preserve terminal state and restore it reliably.
Do not turn txtDesk into SSH, Project Control, Codex, telemetry, or server-control infrastructure.
Keep early implementation small and evidence-driven.
acceptance_conditions: Each milestone is implemented and validated only after its dependencies are complete.
Portability and SSH usability remain explicit validation concerns.
Host-specific deployments remain at the application/provider edge.

glossary.core: generic terminal runtime and desktop framework
glossary.application: a user-facing surface hosted by the desktop
glossary.provider: an adapter to external data or services
glossary.deployment: host-specific selection and policy at the edge

established: txtDesk is a portable host-agnostic terminal desktop.
External and machine-specific semantics belong to applications/providers.
Embedded terminal panes require a mature VT state engine in addition to PTYs.
The plugin boundary remains intentionally unstabilized.
